newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia sees less tourists in Jan-Aug vs 1995.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia sees less tourists in Jan-Aug vs 1995.

text.p: Yugoslavia registered around 2.1 million tourists from January to August this year, or 7.4 percent less than in the same period in 1995, the Yugoslav Statistic Office said in its latest report on Thursday.
Yugoslavs accounted for 1.9 million, or 92 percent of the total, but their numbers dropped 10 percent against the same period last year.
Visitors from other republics of the former Yugoslavia -- Macedonia, Slovenia, Croatia and Bosnia -- accounted for 99,600, increasing by 6.7 percent on the same period in 1995.

A sharp 63 percent rise in the number of foreign visitors was registered in January-August. Of the total 104,800, most came from Russia (12,685), Italy (10,903), Greece (8,685), Bulgaria (7,848) and Germany (7,776).

According to National Bank of Yugoslavia data, hard currency income from tourism in the January-July period stood at $22.3 millilon, or 10 percent less than in the same period last year, the report said. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
